unsure: Scope: the specSym change fixes a pre-existing crash (same-arity overloads differing in an unspecialized parameter type, on any call) that the requested overloaded test shapes hit; it only changes programs that crashed, but the coordinator may prefer it split into its own PR. In the duplicated body, fun.tpe of an explicit super.m[X] TypeApply is an OverloadedType, so the tie-break uses the overloads map, not types. When the matching member of the new parents is missing or still overloaded, the TypeApply case falls back to the old by-symbol select on the stale Super (base behaviour). Overriding a non-polymorphic overload m(b: B) with super.m(b) still loops in a trait or class parent: that is the no-type-argument case of retronym/scala#354, left out of the test.
note: The TypeApply case retypes the Super against the new parents and selects the member matching the variant by symbol (Symbol.matchingSymbol), so overloaded variant names resolve; specSym breaks ties between overloaded variants with the called method's own specialized overload. Body now states the super-from-another-method behaviour change.
